prompt: For every product of brand Sonora and every week whose week_start in calendar falls from 1 to 31 March 2025, how many units of the product were sold that week, from its week_start (a Monday) to the Sunday after? order_ts holds UTC time: use its UTC date. Return three columns, in this order: product_id, week_start and units, with 0 when none were sold. Return one row for each product and week. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per product and week

hints: Next, pair every Sonora product with every week, so that weeks without sales still get a row.
The grid is all products times all weeks; the units come in afterwards through a join that keeps grid rows with no sales.
faded_shape:
WITH weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT week_start FROM calendar WHERE week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-03-01' AND DATE '2025-03-31'),
units AS (SELECT ol.product_id, c.week_start, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN calendar c ON c.cal_date = CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) GROUP BY ol.product_id, c.week_start)
SELECT p.product_id, w.week_start, COALESCE(u.units, 0) AS units
FROM products p
faded_suffix:
LEFT JOIN units u ON u.product_id = p.product_id AND u.week_start = w.week_start
WHERE p.brand = 'Sonora'
why_this_works: CROSS JOIN gives every product every week, and the LEFT JOIN with COALESCE fills a week without sales with 0 instead of dropping it.
